title: FAVIS: Fast and Versatile protocol for metabarcoding of bulk Insect Samples
author: Elżbieta waszkiewicz-Eggebrecht
materials: DNA purification using King Fisher Flex 96 robot For our project we purify a 225 µL aliquot of lysate from each sample using silica-coated magnetic beads with the KingFisher Cell and Tissue DNA kit on a King Fisher Flex 96 robot (both Thermo Scientific) according to manufacturer instructions. You can use alternative kits in your project but make sure you optimize the amount of lysate input needed to obtain enough DNA for your purposes. If you don't have a King Fisher Flex 96 robot, you can purify your DNA manually (see our proposed alternative DNA purification method in step 17 below) but this will take substantially longer to process.
Move all insect bottles to the weighing station.
Wait 5 min until dry (on magnetic stand).

steps.title: Set up washing stations
steps.instruction: Prepare two 80 L plastic containers: one with 10 % bleach (9 parts water + 1 part 47‑50 % NaOCl) and one with soap‑and‑water; keep bleach and soap tanks empty weekly and limit metal exposure to ≤10 min.

steps.title: Create and number work stations
steps.instruction: Divide the bench into 41 stations 30 cm wide, number 1‑41, place a labelled insect bottle at stations 1‑40 and an empty 500 mL Nalgene bottle (blank) at station 41; supply each station with a tray, ethanol‑receiving bottle (500 mL), funnel, bottle seal, two 7 cm nylon mesh circles, and large forceps.

steps.title: Prepare bench cleaning supplies
steps.instruction: Place a squirt bottle filled with 10 % bleach and a paper towel at each station for wiping benches after use.

steps.title: Set up spike‑in station (optional)
steps.instruction: Reserve a clean bench, lay out a petri dish and a dedicated pair of forceps for each spike‑in species; retrieve frozen spike‑ins and place the following numbers into the dishes: D. serrata 1, D. jambulina 1, D. bicornuta 3, S. lateralis 2, G. sigillatus 1, G. bimaculatus 1. Do not add spike‑ins to the blank sample.

steps.title: Set up lysis buffer station
steps.instruction: Arrange graduated cylinders (50‑500 mL), small funnels, pipettes, and filtered tips; pre‑heat lysis buffer bottles in a shaking incubator at 65‑70 °C, 90 rpm, inverting hourly to dissolve salts.

steps.title: Set up weighing station
steps.instruction: Provide precision scales, five coloured stickers (one per biomass category), and a laptop; record the average weight of empty bottles, mesh circles, and labels for later biomass calculations.

steps.title: Pre‑heat insect bottles
steps.instruction: Place all insect bottles in a 60 °C water bath: small bottles (30‑100 mL) for 30 min, large bottles (200‑400 mL) for 40 min, to reach 56 °C before incubation.

steps.title: Incubate bottles at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Transfer pre‑heated bottles to a shaking dry incubator set to 56 °C and 90 rpm; run for the required downstream steps.

steps.title: Optional ethanol concentration check
steps.instruction: While bottles incubate, read preservative ethanol concentration with a density meter if desired.

steps.title: Remove preservative ethanol
steps.instruction: For each station: (a) place one nylon mesh circle over the bottle opening and secure with the bottle seal; (b) pour ≈5 mL ethanol from the bottle through a funnel into the ethanol‑receiving bottle, rotating the bottle to aid drainage; (c) turn the bottle upside down in the funnel and set a 35‑min timer; (d) after 35 min, remove the bottle, discard the mesh, reseal with the original cap; (e) move the funnel to the bleach container for 15 min, then to the soap‑and‑water container.

steps.title: Weigh insect bottles and calculate biomass
steps.instruction: Weigh each bottle, record absolute weight, subtract the pre‑measured weight of bottle + mesh + labels to obtain insect biomass; assign a colour tag according to Table 1 (red 5‑9.99 g, yellow 10‑19.99 g, green 20‑29.99 g, blue 30‑39.99 g, black > 40 g, white < 5 g).

steps.title: Add biological spike‑ins (optional)
steps.instruction: If using spike‑ins, move each sample bottle (except the blank) to the spike‑in station and add the species numbers listed in step 4, then transfer the bottle to the lysis station.

steps.title: Add lysis buffer and proteinase K
steps.instruction: At the lysis station, determine buffer and proteinase K volumes from Table 2 based on the measured biomass; add the calculated amount of lysis buffer (30‑400 mL) to each bottle, rinse walls, then add the matching proteinase K volume (30‑400 µL). Close caps.

steps.title: Incubate lysis reaction
steps.instruction: Place bottles back in the shaking incubator at 56 °C, 90 rpm for 2 h 45 min.

steps.title: Verify ethanol concentration post‑lysis
steps.instruction: Measure ethanol concentration in the receiving bottle with the density meter; if <90 % add 95 % ethanol and repeat measurement until >90 % is achieved.

steps.title: Final bench cleaning
steps.instruction: Wipe all work‑station surfaces with a squirt bottle of 10 % bleach and a paper towel.

steps.title: Collect lysate
steps.instruction: For each bottle: (a) place the second nylon mesh circle, seal with bottle seal; (b) pour lysate slowly into the labelled 250 mL Nalgene lysate collecting bottle; (c) wait until dripping stops and close the lysate bottle; (d) remove the seal, push the mesh back into the insect bottle; (e) re‑attach the original archive label (if present) and refill the bottle with the ethanol removed in step 9, then reseal.

steps.title: Wash station supplies
steps.instruction: Place trays, ethanol‑receiving bottles, seals and forceps into the 10 % bleach container for ≥15 min, then move them to the soap‑and‑water container.

steps.title: Aliquot lysate for DNA purification
steps.instruction: Gather a 1000 µL pipette, filtered tips and a 96‑well microtube rack; gently shake each lysate bottle, then transfer two 900 µL aliquots from each lysate bottle into its corresponding 2 mL microtube; label the rack (A1‑H12) leaving wells H9‑H12 empty for later controls; store lysate bottles and microtubes at –20 °C if not used immediately.

steps.title: Thaw lysate microtubes
steps.instruction: Remove the 96‑well rack from the freezer, thaw at room temperature or in a 37 °C shaking incubator until completely liquid and well‑mixed.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to deep‑well plate
steps.instruction: Open each microtube and pipette 225 µL into the corresponding well of a 96‑well deep‑well plate (2.2 mL capacity); add 225 µL ddH₂O to well H9 (negative control) and 225 µL of a known‑DNA lysate to well H10 (positive control); leave wells H11 and H12 empty for library‑prep controls.

steps.title: Magnetic‑bead DNA purification (optional)
steps.instruction: Prepare magnetic bead solution and fresh 80 % ethanol; for each well add 40 µL PCR product + 80 µL beads, mix, incubate 5 min RT, magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 150 µL 80 % ethanol (1 min each, magnet between washes), dry 5 min, elute with 100 µL TE (or water if EDTA‑sensitive); split eluate: 40 µL to storage plate, 40 µL to working DNA plate; store plates at –20 °C (storage) and 4 °C (working).

steps.title: Prepare PCR 1 master mix
steps.instruction: For a 96‑well plate (95 samples + 1 negative): multiply per‑well volumes by 95. Per well: 4 µL 10 µM COI BF3 mix, 4 µL 10 µM COI BR2 mix, 68 µL ddH₂O, 4 µL DNA template (or ddH₂O for negative). Total 40 µL per well. Run PCR: 95 °C 900 s; 25 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 50 °C 90 s, 72 °C 90 s; final extension 72 °C 600 s; hold.

steps.title: Clean up PCR 1 products
steps.instruction: Transfer 20 µL PCR 1 product to a 96‑well plate, add 40 µL magnetic bead solution (2×), mix, incubate 5 min RT, magnet 2 min, discard supernatant, wash twice with 150 µL 80 % ethanol (1 min each, magnet between), dry 5 min, add 20.5 µL TE, mix, centrifuge, magnet 2 min, transfer 20 µL eluate to a new plate, label and store at 4 °C (short‑term) or –20 °C (long‑term).

steps.title: Prepare PCR 2 master mix
steps.instruction: For a 96‑well plate (95 samples + 1 negative) multiply per‑well volumes by 100. Per well: 0.7 µL 10 µM Index i5, 0.7 µL 10 µM Index i7, 22 µL ddH₂O, 0.5 µL PCR 1 product (or ddH₂O for negative). Total 10 µL per well. Run PCR: 95 °C 90 s; 6‑7 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 50 °C 90 s, 72 °C 90 s; final extension 72 °C 600 s; hold.

steps.title: Check PCR 2 products on gel
steps.instruction: Load 2 µL PCR 2 product mixed with 2 µL loading dye onto a 2.5 % agarose gel and run to verify band size.

steps.title: Clean plate pools with magnetic beads
steps.instruction: Combine PCR 2 products from each 96‑well plate into a 1.5 mL tube proportionally to gel intensity (strong 1 µL, medium 2 µL, weak 4 µL, none 8 µL); clean each pool with ProNex beads at 1:1.5 (v/v) using 80 µL pool; measure concentration on Qubit.

steps.title: Create master pools A and B
steps.instruction: Based on Qubit concentrations, mix four plate pools (384 libraries) to form Master Pool A and another four to form Master Pool B (each 384 libraries); measure each master pool on Qubit, then clean again with ProNex beads at 1:1.3 (v/v), eluting in TE 0.1 × or ddH₂O to the desired final concentration.

steps.title: Assess library quality
steps.instruction: Run each Master Pool on a Bioanalyzer or TapeStation to check for primer‑dimer contamination and overall size distribution before sequencing.

steps.title: Sequencing plan
steps.instruction: Pool 768 libraries (8 × 96‑well plates) for NovaSeq SPrime 2 × 250 bp flow cell; load Master Pool A and B (384 libraries each) into separate lanes; expect >500 bp reads, ~1 M read pairs per library.
